name: Battle of Kursk
note: The plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: the formations are armies and fronts, drawn as simple blocks. The accounts give the northern face, the southern face, Orel to the north and Belgorod and Prokhorovka but not their distances, so the places are set by judgement. The Northern Donets is drawn as a line south of the 4th Panzer Army and Army Detachment Kempf; the accounts do not say exactly where it lay. Ponyri and Olkhovatka are placed on the northern face without exact positions. The 7th Guards Army, which faced Army Detachment Kempf, is not drawn apart from the Voronezh Front.

phases.title: The two armies take up their ground
phases.text: The Germans planned two pincers on the Kursk salient, the 9th Army from the north and the 4th Panzer Army with Army Detachment Kempf from the south, while the 2nd Army held the west. The Central and Voronezh Fronts stood in fortified belts, with the Steppe Front in reserve.
phases.quote: Operation Citadel called for a double envelopment to surround the Soviet defenders of five armies and seal off the Kursk salient.

phases.title: The 9th Army attacks in the north
phases.text: The 9th Army opened its attack on the Central Front at 05:30 after a preliminary bombardment. It broke into the first belt of the Soviet defences and reached the small town of Ponyri in the second belt on the first day.
phases.quote: Following a preliminary bombardment and Red Army counter bombardments, the 9th Army opened its attack at 05:30 on 5 July.

phases.title: The southern pincer attacks
phases.text: In the south the 4th Panzer Army and Army Detachment Kempf attacked the Voronezh Front after a bombardment. By the end of the day a wedge had been created in the first belt of the Soviet defences.
phases.quote: By the end of 5 July, a wedge had been created in the first belt of the Soviet defences.

phases.title: The Central Front counterattacks and holds
phases.text: The Soviet 16th Tank Corps counterattacked and was forced back by Tiger tanks. The Germans then attacked at Olkhovatka and Ponyri, but the Central Front held both places.
phases.quote: but it failed to break the Red Army defence at Olkhovatka, and the Germans suffered heavy casualties.

phases.title: The northern attack is halted at Ponyri
phases.text: Model put the weight of the 9th Army on Ponyri and Olkhovatka, and control of Ponyri changed hands several times. By 10 July the Soviets had completely halted the German advance in the north.
phases.quote: By 10 July, the Soviets had completely halted the German advance.

phases.title: The 5th Guards Tank Army moves to Prokhorovka
phases.text: The 5th Guards Tank Army, from the Steppe Front, began advancing to Prokhorovka to reinforce the Voronezh Front.
phases.quote: On 7 July, the 5th Guards Tank Army began advancing to Prokhorovka.

phases.title: The Voronezh Front counterattacks in pieces
phases.text: Vatutin ordered a counterattack on the II SS Panzer Corps, but poor coordination made it a series of piecemeal attacks. It still stalled the II SS Panzer Corps for the day.
phases.quote: Although a fiasco, the Soviet counterattack succeeded in stalling the advance of the II SS Panzer Corps throughout the day.

phases.title: The II SS Panzer Corps turns to Prokhorovka
phases.text: Hoth turned the II SS Panzer Corps of the 4th Panzer Army away from Oboyan to attack north-east towards Prokhorovka. This move had been part of the plan since the start of the offensive.
phases.quote: At this point, Hoth turned the II SS Panzer Corps away from Oboyan to attack toward the northeast in the direction of Prokhorovka.

phases.title: Army Detachment Kempf breaks through
phases.text: In a surprise night attack the 6th Panzer Division seized a bridge across the Donets. Army Detachment Kempf then pushed troops across for an advance on Prokhorovka from the south.
phases.quote: On 11 July, Army Detachment Kempf finally achieved a breakthrough.

phases.title: The tank battle at Prokhorovka
phases.text: The 5th Guards Tank Army attacked down the slopes before Prokhorovka against the II SS Panzer Corps, which was attacking on its own plan. Neither side accomplished its objectives that day.
phases.quote: Down off the west slopes, before Prokhorovka, came the massed armour of five tank brigades from the Soviet 18th and 29th Tank Corps of the 5th Guards Tank Army.

phases.title: Operation Kutuzov opens against the Orel salient
phases.text: The Bryansk and Western Fronts began Operation Kutuzov against the Orel salient. The thrusts endangered German supply routes and threatened the 9th Army with encirclement, so that it went over fully to the defensive.
phases.quote: These thrusts endangered German supply routes and threatened the 9th Army with encirclement.

phases.title: The II SS Panzer Corps ends its offensive
phases.text: The southern offensive went on with Operation Roland from 14 July. On 17 July the II SS Panzer Corps was ordered to end its offensive operations and begin to withdraw.
phases.quote: the II SS Panzer Corps was ordered to end its offensive operations and begin to withdraw

phases.title: Operation Rumyantsev drives south to Belgorod
phases.text: The Voronezh and Steppe Fronts attacked the northern wing of Army Group South, aiming to destroy the 4th Panzer Army and Army Detachment Kempf. They drove through the German positions and by 5 August had liberated Belgorod.
phases.quote: The offensive was initiated by the Voronezh Front and Steppe Fronts against the northern wing of Army Group South.
